t: For an additional amount to enable the Secretary of Transportation to make a grant to the National Railroad Passenger Corporation, $21,500,000 is hereby appropriated which shall be available until expended for capital improvements associated with safety-related emergency repairs at the existing Pennsylvania Station in New York City: Provided, That none of the funds herein appropriated shall be used for the redevelopment of the James A. Farley Post Office Building in New York City as a train station and commercial center: Provided further, That the $21,500,000 shall be considered part of the Federal cost share for the redevelopment of the James A. Farley Post Office Building, if authorized.

fable.w: This section only appropriates funds for a grant to Amtrak for safety repairs at Pennsylvania Station and limits how the funds may be used and counted. The tempting reading is that a grant to an outside corporation involves an outside party, but grants are not participation under the definition. There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: For an additional amount to enable the Secretary of Transportation to make a grant to the National Railroad Passenger Corporation, $21,500,000 is hereby appropriated

qwen_block.w: This section is an appropriation provision that authorizes the Secretary of Transportation to make a grant to the National Railroad Passenger Corporation. It does not require consultation, coordination, or participation with any outside parties (such as the public, states, or tribes) before making a decision. The definition explicitly excludes applications for grants and intra-governmental actions. The National Railroad Passenger Corporation (Amtrak) is a federally chartered corporation, and even if considered outside, the text merely authorizes a grant payment rather than establishing a participatory process like a hearing or advisory committee.
qwen_block.s: For an additional amount to enable the Secretary of Transportation to make a grant to the National Railroad Passenger Corporation, $21,500,000 is hereby appropriated

opus.w: This section is an appropriation that funds a grant to Amtrak and restricts how the money can be spent. The definition excludes grants, and the section never requires outside parties to be consulted before a federal decision. Amtrak's involvement as the grant recipient might look like participation, but receiving funds is not taking part in a federal decision.
opus.s: For an additional amount to enable the Secretary of Transportation to make a grant to the National Railroad Passenger Corporation, $21,500,000 is hereby appropriated
opus.b:
**Step 1: Analysis.** The tempting reading is that this counts as participation because an outside entity, the National Railroad Passenger Corporation (Amtrak), receives a federal grant and is involved in the Pennsylvania Station project. That reading fails the definition. The section only appropriates money and limits how it can be used. The definition excludes grants. Nothing here has the Secretary consulting Amtrak, the public, states, or any other outside party before making a decision. There is also no hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.

**Step 2: Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes an appropriation for a grant to the National Railroad Passenger Corporation. It sets conditions on the use of funds but does not require the federal government to consult or coordinate with outside parties (such as the public, states, or independent experts) before making a decision. The definition excludes applications for grants, and this text describes the funding mechanism rather than a participatory decision-making process involving non-federal actors.
qwen_chat.s: For an additional amount to enable the Secretary of Transportation to make a grant to the National Railroad Passenger Corporation, $21,500,000 is hereby appropriated which shall be available until expended for capital improvements associated with safety-related emergency repairs at the existing Pennsylvania Station in New York City: Provided, That none of the funds herein appropriated shall be used for the redevelopment of the James A. Farley Post Office Building in New York City as a train station and commercial center: Provided further, That the $21,500,000 shall be considered part of the Federal cost share for the redevelopment of the James A. Farley Post Office Building, if authorized.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the funds are for a specific project involving a corporation (Amtrak) and potentially a post office building, there is an implicit requirement for coordination or consultation with outside parties. However, the text itself only authorizes an appropriation and sets conditions on its use (e.g., not for redevelopment). It does not mandate any process where the federal government consults with or coordinates with outside entities before making a decision. The grant is to a specific entity, but the act of granting or the conditions listed do not constitute "participation" as defined (consultation, advisory boards with non-federal members, public hearings, etc.). The definition explicitly excludes applications for grants, and this section is about the appropriation for a grant, not a participatory process.
